hook.speaker: Bhartrihari
hook.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
hook.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
hook.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
hook.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
hook.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
alternates.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
alternates.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
alternates.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

alternates.speaker: Kausalya
alternates.setting: Holding back tears, Kausalya blesses her son before he leaves for fourteen years in the forest.
alternates.sanskrit: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥
alternates.line: May the good you have lived by, gladly and faithfully, now protect you.
alternates.translation: May the goodness you have kept so gladly and so faithfully protect you, tiger of the Raghus.
alternates.misuse: A mother's blessing, not a promise that good people never suffer.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

why: Two sources of the mind's pain (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Ashma Gita))

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Poem 'Hold On Yet a While, Brave Heart', written to the Maharaja of Khetri.
verse.line: Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come.
verse.translation: If the sun by the cloud is hidden a bit, If the welkin shows but gloom, Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come. … Not a work will be lost, no struggle vain, Though hopes be blighted, powers gone; … Then hold on yet a while, brave soul, No good is e'er undone.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.for_you: You are in the season where things are turning, and this is the ground to hold. The work you are doing now has a future you cannot yet see. Keep going.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing today that seems hidden but is still working.
verse.scene_line: You stand beside the Maharaja of Khetri as the clouds hide the sun, waiting for the light.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: तृणोल्कया ज्ञायते जातरूपं / वृत्तेन भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः / शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः / कृच्छ्रेष्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश्च
verse.line: Gold shows in fire, character in conduct, courage in danger, and true friends in hard times.
verse.translation: Gold is known by a flame of straw; a good person by conduct, an honest one by dealings, a brave one in danger, a steady one in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times.
verse.why: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: Keshini's choice and the tests of character
prasang.summary: Vidura tells how Prahlada judged honestly against his own son when Princess Keshini set two suitors a test, then gives aphorisms: gold is tested by fire, friends by hard times, and a clear conscience lets you sleep.
prasang.lesson: Character shows under pressure. Do by day what will let you sleep at night.

verse.for_you: The good you have built shows in the small, steady choices you make. Stay with the work, and the true circle around you will only grow clearer. Keep the flame of your resolve lit today.
verse.try_today: Notice one small act of integrity in your day.

why: Explains why hard times thin out one's circle
Hardship is recast as the test that shows what is real

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The graduation address as a student leaves to start family life.
verse.sanskrit: वेदमनूच्याचार्योन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।
verse.line: Speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning.
verse.translation: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the student: Speak the truth. Practise what is right. Do not neglect your study.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.for_you: You are stepping into a life where truth and right action meet. Keep your learning open as the days unfold.
verse.try_today: Notice one small truth you speak today.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the threshold, ready to teach what you have learned.

why: study is to be kept up, not finished
three plain commitments to carry into working life

verse.speaker: Parvati
verse.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
verse.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
verse.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
verse.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
verse.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
verse.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

verse.for_you: You have chosen a path and the gold of it is already showing. Let your resolve hold, even when the body asks for rest. This is your nature now, and it will not break.
verse.try_today: Notice when your body asks for rest and let your resolve hold anyway.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of your chosen path, like gold in the fire, holding to what you are.

story.title: The glory of the Gita
story.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.
story.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.
story.for_you: You are already turning the corner. The field is the same, but your sight is clear. You will meet it with steady hands.
